boj-press-2026-01-23-ueda-kk260126a-p01: As for the conduct of monetary policy, given that real interest rates are currently at significantly low levels, if the outlook for economic activity and prices presented so far is realized, the Bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation in accordance with improvement in economic activity and prices.
boj-press-2026-01-23-ueda-kk260126a-p02: It is likely to take considerable time for the effects of policy changes to spread widely through the real economy and prices via these financial conditions, but the Bank intends to examine carefully the various effects, including those of past rate hikes, on the behavior of firms and households and on economic activity and prices.
boj-press-2026-02-06-masu-kk260209a-p01: I only meant that, as a matter of course, the Bank must not derail the economy with excessive rate hikes; I do not think we are behind the curve at this stage either, and what I said was simply that we want to proceed carefully while weighing both sides.
boj-press-2026-02-06-masu-kk260209a-p02: Keeping underlying inflation at 2% is not meant as tightening for its own sake; it is not desirable for inflation to stay above 2%, so if that happens, we would have to move toward tightening. You can take it exactly that way.
boj-press-2026-02-26-takata-kk260227a-p0: On the point you raised, I myself have been saying since last year that the price stability target has more or less been achieved, and in that sense I already proposed a rate hike at the January meeting this year. Whatever happens from here, I would first like to make clear that this is my stance.

As I mentioned, I also called for a rate hike in January this year, and behind that is my view that overseas developments have a very large influence. In today's speech I described 2026 as a turning point toward recovery, so I want to respond taking full account of that, looking not only at the domestic situation but even more at conditions overseas.
boj-press-2026-03-02-himino-kk260303a-p0: Accommodative financial conditions may well be one of the background factors, so we need to watch asset price developments closely, but I do not think the current situation requires any particular response from monetary policy.

We want to judge as accurately as possible what effects rate hikes would have depending on how far and when we raise rates. But as with underlying inflation and the natural rate of interest, this cannot be pinned down precisely at any point in time. In terms of what I said today, I think it is better to look at the whole mandala and assess everything together, rather than picking out one part and deciding that because it has reached a certain point, it is time to act.
boj-press-2026-03-19-ueda-kk260323a-p01: As for the conduct of monetary policy, given that real interest rates are currently at significantly low levels, if the outlook for economic activity and prices presented so far is realized, the Bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation in accordance with improvement in economic activity and prices.
boj-press-2026-03-19-ueda-kk260323a-p02: We also need to pay attention to the effect of higher crude oil prices on the outlook for underlying inflation.
boj-press-2026-04-01-asada-kk260402a-p01: I have long supported and valued that policy, so I have no problem with being called a reflationist in that sense.
boj-press-2026-04-01-asada-kk260402a-p02: In that case, it is quite difficult to deal with it through monetary policy.
boj-press-2026-04-16-ueda-kk260420a-p01: Looking ahead to the coming Monetary Policy Meetings, as I always say, higher crude oil prices first put downward pressure on the economy by worsening the terms of trade.
boj-press-2026-04-28-ueda-kk260430a-p01: Both of these risks could rise together, but with underlying inflation approaching 2% and firms' wage- and price-setting behavior becoming more active, we need to pay close attention in particular to the risk that inflation overshoots significantly and that this then harms the economy.
boj-press-2026-04-28-ueda-kk260430a-p02: On prices, the economic slowdown caused by the situation in the Middle East will push down on underlying inflation through a worsening output gap, but overall we think the upside risks are larger.
boj-press-2026-04-28-ueda-kk260430a-p03: With underlying inflation approaching 2% and real interest rates currently at significantly low levels, the Bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation in accordance with economic activity, prices and financial conditions.
boj-press-2026-05-19-ueda-kk260522b-p01: On inflation expectations, I cannot yet say anything definitive, but firms' views on prices in the Tankan, although a little dated, and recent moves in break-even inflation rates show some upward drift, so we want to watch this closely.
boj-press-2026-05-21-koeda-kk260522a-p01: So by a moderate pace I mean that, at present, I see raising the policy interest rate at a moderate pace, and responding to high prices through monetary policy as well, as the appropriate policy, while taking the trade-offs for the economy into account.
boj-press-2026-05-21-koeda-kk260522a-p02: As for the neutral rate, which of course has to be seen as a range, I currently see its lower bound as above 1%.
boj-press-2026-05-21-koeda-kk260522a-p03: Upside risks to prices have, I think, already materialized, particularly in business-to-business prices.
boj-press-2026-06-16-uchida-kk260617a-p0: As for the future conduct of monetary policy, with underlying inflation approaching 2% and financial conditions currently accommodative, the Bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation in accordance with economic activity, prices and financial conditions.

Meanwhile, with the effects of government measures such as energy cost relief expected to continue, and alternative sourcing of raw materials heavily dependent on the Middle East making progress, we think the risk of a major downturn in the economy has fallen compared with a while ago.
boj-press-2026-06-25-tamura-kk260626a-p0: My own view at present is that the 2% price stability target has already been achieved, and that to prevent underlying inflation from rising above 2%, the policy interest rate needs to be raised to around the neutral rate.
If underlying inflation rose above 2%, bringing it down would require raising the policy interest rate sharply and substantially into restrictive territory and holding it there for a long time.
boj-press-2026-06-30-sato-kk260701a-p01: It is important to pay attention to both the downside risks to the economy and the upside risks to inflation; we have to watch both closely.
boj-press-2026-06-30-sato-kk260701a-p02: On your second point, the exit: the Bank is currently normalizing monetary policy, and if you ask whether we have inflation or deflation, some upside risk to inflation may be observed, but I do not think it is yet very strong as a norm. I will continue to listen carefully to the staff's explanations and examine the data in my own way.
boj-press-2026-07-31-ueda-kk260803a-p01: With underlying inflation approaching 2% and financial conditions currently accommodative, the Bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation in accordance with economic activity, prices and financial conditions.
boj-press-2026-07-31-ueda-kk260803a-p02: In particular, we think it will become important to stabilize underlying inflation at around 2%, so that the risk of it overshooting the 2% price stability target does not materialize and then harm the economy.
boj-press-2026-08-27-himino-kk260828a-p0: In particular, given that underlying inflation is now approaching 2%, I think we need to be more conscious of upside risks to prices than before, and on that basis we intend to examine economic activity, prices and financial conditions and discuss them thoroughly at every Monetary Policy Meeting.

As for the timing and pace of rate hikes you asked about, we intend to consider them while examining the likelihood of the baseline outlook being realized and the risks, including the effects of the situation in the Middle East, growing AI-related demand and exchange rate movements.
boj-press-2026-09-01-ueda-kk260904a-p01: Let me repeat the basic thinking I set out then: on the timing and pace of adjusting the degree of monetary accommodation, we will consider them while examining the likelihood of the baseline outlook for economic activity and prices being realized and the surrounding risks, putting particular weight on the three points I mentioned, the situation in the Middle East, AI-related developments and the effects of exchange rate movements.
boj-press-2026-09-02-takata-kk260903a-p0: That is the background to my proposal for a rate hike in July.

Given developments overseas and at home, and the increase in lending and other financial activity under accommodative conditions, the situation calls not for the earlier pace of once every six months, twice a year, but for a nimble response suited to the new circumstances.
boj-press-2026-09-10-masu-kk260911a-p01: On the neutral rate, which I knew I would be asked about: nobody knows exactly where it is, and as with what I just said, we will look at it carefully each time. Whether we would respond in the particular way you describe also has to be judged as we go, but I think we will proceed as before, watching carefully.
boj-press-2026-09-18-ueda-kk260924a-p01: As for the future conduct of monetary policy, with underlying inflation approaching 2% and financial conditions currently accommodative, the Bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation in accordance with economic activity, prices and financial conditions.
boj-press-2026-09-18-ueda-kk260924a-p02: In particular, we think it will become important to stabilize underlying inflation at around 2%, so that the risk of it overshooting the 2% price stability target does not materialize and then harm the economy.
boj-press-2026-10-15-koeda-kk261016a-p01: On your second question, about future rate hikes: where we stand now is that financial conditions are accommodative.
boj-press-2026-10-15-koeda-kk261016a-p02: Given that, I think it is appropriate to adjust the policy interest rate in a timely and appropriate manner, keeping the estimated range of the neutral rate in mind while examining economic, price and financial conditions.
boj-press-2026-10-16-ueda-kk261020a-p01: As for the implications for our policy, I can only state our basic stance: with underlying inflation approaching 2% while financial conditions, as I always say, remain accommodative, the Bank will basically continue to raise the policy interest rate and adjust the degree of accommodation, in accordance with economic activity, prices and financial conditions.
boj-press-2026-10-16-ueda-kk261020a-p02: This overlaps with what I said at the press conference after the September meeting: with underlying inflation very close to 2%, stabilizing it at around 2% is becoming more important than before.
